title: The Mendoza Estate

story.narrative: Arturo Mendoza died leaving a surviving spouse, Elena, and two legitimate-child lines: Beatriz and the line of his predeceased son Carlos, represented by Daniela and Emilio. In his will, Arturo devised his Quezon City condominium to Beatriz and left a monetary legacy to Lucia Ramos. The exercise asks how the net estate, compulsory shares, representation, devise, and legacy fit together.
story.circumstances: For this classroom exercise, the marriage, filiation, and will are assumed valid. Carlos predeceased Arturo; no prior donations, disinheritance, or other compulsory heirs are stated.
keyFacts: Carlos died before Arturo, leaving Daniela and Emilio.
The condominium is subject to an outstanding mortgage.
Lucia Ramos is a legatee and is not presented as a compulsory heir.

properties.name: Quezon City condominium
properties.description: A residential condominium exclusively owned by the testator.

properties.name: Mabuhay Foods shares
properties.description: Unlisted corporate shares valued for the exercise.

properties.name: Bank and cash accounts
properties.description: Cash available for satisfying monetary allocations.

dispositions.description: Arturo devises the condominium to Beatriz. Its exercise value is treated as covering her legitime and part of the disposable portion.
Arturo gives Lucia a monetary legacy of PHP 1,500,000 from the disposable portion.

expectedDistribution.rationale: The surviving spouse receives an amount equal to the legitime of one legitimate-child line.
The condominium has a net exercise value of PHP 7,500,000. PHP 4,500,000 covers Beatriz's legitime and PHP 3,000,000 is charged to the disposable portion.
Daniela receives one-half of Carlos's PHP 4,500,000 line share by representation.
Emilio receives one-half of Carlos's PHP 4,500,000 line share by representation.
The monetary legacy is charged to the remaining disposable portion.

explanation: Fictitious educational scenario. The net hereditary estate is PHP 18,000,000. Under Article 888, the collective legitime of the two legitimate-child lines is one-half, or PHP 9,000,000, giving PHP 4,500,000 per line. Under Article 892, the surviving spouse receives PHP 4,500,000 from the disposable portion. Carlos's PHP 4,500,000 line share is divided per stirpes between Daniela and Emilio under Articles 970-974. The remaining PHP 4,500,000 disposable portion supports PHP 3,000,000 of Beatriz's devise above her legitime and Lucia's PHP 1,500,000 legacy. Assumptions: valid will and marriage, established filiation, no disinheritance, no prior donations requiring collation, and stated values are net for this classroom exercise. This is not legal advice.

source.title: Civil Code of the Philippines, Articles 888, 892, and 970-974
